comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Total elongation of triplex low-density steels relative to commercially available steel grades of similar tensile strength

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The 'annealed' part of the 'Annealed and aged' processing condition given for the Triplex steel in Table I. The general triplex processing route involves solution annealing in a two-phase (α + γ) or three-phase (α + γ + κ-carbide) field followed by quenching.

The 'aged' part of the 'Annealed and aged' processing condition given for the Triplex steel in Table I. The general triplex route involves an aging step after solution annealing/quenching to form the triplex (α + γ + κ-carbide) microstructure.

structures.overall_structure: Triplex microstructure consisting of ferrite (α), austenite (γ), and κ-carbide

unmapped_findings: Strain hardening exponent n = 0.16 (marked with 'b', i.e., determined by the current authors from the data provided in reference 32) is reported for the Triplex steel in Table I. [b0066]
Uniform elongation (UE) and normal anisotropy factor (r̄) are not reported (shown as '-') for the Triplex steel in Table I. [b0066]

The banana diagram (Fig. 9) places 'Fe-Mn-Al-C Triplex steels (γ + α + κ)' as a class at roughly 800–1050 MPa UTS and 45–75% total elongation, with Fe-Mn-Al-C density reduction of 10–20%; this is a class-level range, not a measured value for this specific sample. [b0052, figure_009]

The Triplex sample shares the same nominal composition Fe-5.8Al-3.5Mn-0.35C and 'Annealed and aged' processing label with the ferrite-based duplex sample in Table I, but differs in final phase constitution (triplex α + γ + κ-carbide vs duplex α + γ). [b0066]
